group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 56-year-old man who resides on the medical wing of a long-term care facility was transferred to the emergency department in the early afternoon after staff noticed that he had developed a harsh, productive cough overnight accompanied by shaking chills and a single recorded tympanic temperature of 39.4 °C despite scheduled acetaminophen being held for the past twenty-four hours. According to the hand-off note, he is normally able to propel his own wheelchair to meals and recreational activities, manages bathing with minimal assistance, and routinely converses clearly with staff and other residents; no baseline cognitive impairment is documented, and the nurse accompanying him reported that he was “his usual self” during the ambulance ride. His medical background is notable for biopsy-proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis with bridging fibrosis diagnosed three years earlier; he sees hepatology every six months, has never experienced ascites or encephalopathy, and his most recent outpatient laboratory panel eight weeks ago showed preserved synthetic function except for mildly elevated transaminases. He has long-standing hypertension treated with amlodipine 10 mg daily and lisinopril 5 mg, but he has never been told he has weak heart muscle, valve disease, or fluid overload and he remains free of orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or lower-extremity edema. He denies any prior kidney problems, has never required nephrology consultation, and his serum creatinine has been stable around 0.8–0.9 mg/dL on facility checks; he has also never undergone chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or tumor resection, and no family member has mentioned concern for malignancy. He quit smoking cigarettes two decades ago after a 12-pack-year exposure, drinks no alcohol because of his liver condition, and has never used illicit drugs. He received both pneumococcal vaccines last year and the current season’s influenza vaccine, and he has not taken antibiotics in the preceding twelve months. Medications taken with breakfast this morning included the two antihypertensives noted above, vitamin D, and lactulose 10 g as bowel regulator; he had not ingested any antipyretics, steroids, bronchodilators, or diuretics before presentation. On arrival he sat upright on the stretcher, speaking in full sentences, oriented to name, location, date, and current events, and he answered all questions appropriately without slurred speech or hesitation. Triage vital signs recorded prior to any intervention revealed an oral temperature of 39.4 °C, heart rate 86 beats/min with a regular rhythm, non-invasive blood pressure 121/74 mm Hg, respiratory rate 36 breaths/min with shallow excursions and faint intercostal retractions, and pulse oximetry 92 % breathing ambient air. His skin was warm and flushed, conjunctivae were anicteric, and capillary refill was brisk; jugular venous contour was not distended at 45°. Cardiac auscultation disclosed a crisp S1 and S2 without murmurs, gallops, or rubs. Pulmonary examination revealed markedly reduced breath sounds and dullness to percussion over the left posterior lower third of the thorax with coarse crackles just above that level; no wheezes were heard on forced expiration. The abdomen was soft and non-distended, with a firm but nontender liver edge palpable two centimeters below the right costal margin; there was no shifting dullness or peripheral stigmata of chronic liver disease other than mild palmar erythema. Extremities were warm, without edema, and distal pulses were symmetric. Screening neurologic assessment showed equal pupils, intact extraocular movements, fluent speech, 5/5 strength in all major muscle groups, normal sensation to light touch, and steady finger-nose-finger testing. Point-of-care capillary glucose measured 117 mg/dL. Venous blood was drawn and an arterial sample obtained from the radial artery within ten minutes of stretcher placement, both prior to any intravenous fluids, antimicrobials, or supplemental oxygen. Initial laboratory results demonstrated sodium 150 mEq/L, potassium 3.8 mEq/L, chloride 104 mEq/L, bicarbonate 26 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 14 mg/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, and hematocrit 32 %. White blood cell count was 13.1 × 10⁹/L with 85 % neutrophils, and platelet count was 220 × 10⁹/L. Liver panel showed AST 74 U/L, ALT 68 U/L, total bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL, albumin 3.5 g/dL, and INR 1.2, consistent with his chronic hepatic condition. An arterial blood gas obtained on room air revealed pH 7.52, PaCO₂ 31 mm Hg, PaO₂ 81 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 25 mEq/L. Portable postero-anterior and lateral chest radiographs taken before any therapy displayed a dense consolidation involving the left lower lobe with a meniscus-shaped opacity blunting the left costophrenic angle, suggestive of an accompanying pleural fluid collection; the heart appeared normal in size, mediastinum was midline, and the right lung fields were clear. Electrocardiography performed immediately afterward showed normal sinus rhythm at 84 beats/min, normal intervals, and no ischemic changes. Two sets of blood cultures, expectorated sputum for Gram stain and culture, and a multiplex respiratory viral panel were collected before antibiotics were ordered. At the moment this note is written, he has received no intravenous fluids other than the small heparinized flush used for the arterial line, no antipyretics, no oxygen beyond ambient air, and no antimicrobial agents, thereby preserving the above measurements as his untreated baseline.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) adds demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points using untreated admission findings.
- Demographics: a man starts with his age in years (56 points); long-term care residence adds 10.
- Comorbidities: biopsy-proven chronic liver disease adds 20 despite preserved synthetic function. No documented malignancy, heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, or renal disease: 0 each.
- Examination: respiratory rate 36/min meets the ≥30 threshold (+20). He is oriented, systolic BP is 121 (not <90), temperature is 39.4°C (neither <35 nor ≥40), and pulse is 86 (not ≥125): 0 each.
- Laboratory findings: pH 7.52 is not <7.35; BUN 14 is not ≥30 mg/dL; sodium 150 is not <130 mEq/L; glucose 117 is not ≥250 mg/dL; hematocrit 32% is not <30%; room-air PaO₂ 81 mm Hg is not <60. Each scores 0.
- Radiograph: left pleural effusion adds 10.
PSI = 56 + 10 + 20 + 20 + 10 = 116.
Final answer: 116
